Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

After several SOLD OUT workshops in Wellington here is the next one... Nov 2026

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Sunday 1st November - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2 - 4pm




Ema Frost is a very clever Kiwi Artist, who has been teaching Kintsugi for 5+ years and regularly travels to Japan to study and learn new techniques. Ema's illustrations and ceramic works sit in many of our countries best galleries, and whose products and merchandise sell in the most stylish design stores and gallery shops. Her style is enchanting - quirky, feminine and colourful, and clearly influenced by her travels throughout the world, usually off the beaten track.

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.

KintsugiIt's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:A finished artwork pieceA understanding of KintsugiKnowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Overview

Helping managers and people leaders in New Zealand regulatory agencies navigate AI-enabled change with confidence.

Programme Details
Dates: Wednesday, 18 November & Thursday, 19 November
Time: 9:00 am – 1:00 pm daily (2-day interactive workshop)
Location: MartinJenkins, Wellington
Investment: $1,400 + GST per seat
Capacity: Strictly limited to 10 participants to ensure an interactive, small-group experience.
Facilitators: Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths
The Leadership Challenge

Artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities across the public sector, but technology is only part of the story. For many leaders, the immediate challenge is helping people adapt. Teams are asking questions about changing work practices, emerging capabilities, workforce impacts, and what these changes mean for their day-to-day roles.

Leaders are increasingly expected to communicate clearly, manage uncertainty, respond to concerns, maintain engagement, and support learning while organisational approaches continue to evolve.

Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change has been designed to help people leaders meet these challenges. Rather than teaching AI tools, the programme focuses on the practical leadership skills needed to guide teams through change.

Who This Programme Is For

This programme is designed specifically for people leaders within New Zealand regulatory agencies and public sector bodies, including:

Managers
Team leaders
Anyone responsible for supporting people through organisational change

No technical background or AI expertise is required.

What Participants Will Gain

By the end of the programme, participants will be better equipped to:

Understand the unique people impacts of AI-enabled change
Recognise and address common concerns and resistance
Lead teams through uncertainty and ambiguity
Build confidence and trust during periods of change
Communicate effectively about emerging technologies and organisational shifts
Support adaptation, continuous learning, and experimentation
Apply practical leadership approaches immediately within their own teams




Programme Structure
Day 1: Understanding the change and leading through uncertainty

Wednesday, 18 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

Leaders explore the people impacts of AI-enabled change and their role in guiding teams through it. They will understand how to assess readiness, communicate honestly, and build psychological safety in regulatory and public sector settings.

What will be covered
The leadership context for AI-driven change
How people respond to change and uncertainty
Change readiness and leadership responsibilities
Building trust through clear, credible communication
Crafting messages leaders can use with their teams
Reflecting on risks and opportunities in own context
Day 2: Engaging teams and turning change into action

Thursday, 19 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

The focus shifts from understanding change to leading it. This will include sustaining engagement and motivation, applying frameworks to real situations, and leaving with a practical plan for adoption.

What will be covered
Team engagement and motivation during change
Applying practical change leadership frameworks
Responding to resistance, fear and scepticism
Supporting learning and capability development
Safe experimentation and responsible adoption
Pulse checks, action planning and next steps




Learning Approach

This is a highly interactive, small-group programme built around:

Facilitated discussion
Real public sector examples
Practical leadership tools and frameworks
Small-group exercises and peer learning
Application to participants' own workplace contexts

Participants are encouraged to bring current challenges and opportunities from their own organisations.

Why This Programme Is Different

Many AI learning programmes focus purely on technology and software tools. Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change focuses on the leadership challenge.

Successful adoption of new technologies depends on people. This programme equips leaders with practical approaches for helping teams adapt, engage, learn, and perform during periods of transformation.

About the Facilitators

Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths

This programme combines deep expertise in change leadership and AI transformation. Cat Moody and Jarred Griffiths bring practical experience supporting public sector organisations through organisational change, workforce transitions, leadership development, and AI adoption.

Participants will benefit from real examples, lessons learned, and practical insights drawn from current, hands-on work across public sector agencies.

Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

A guided kundalini activation. Breath of fire and kundalini pranayama, simple repetitive movement, sound and stillness, sequenced to wake up energy that has been sitting dormant along the spine and let it move.

Who is this for

People who already have some breathwork or movement practice and want something more activating than a wind-down class. You are curious about kundalini but want it held by someone who works with the nervous system, not bypasses it. You are willing to feel a lot and stop when you need to.

Not the right fit as a first-ever breathwork experience. The Root or a gentler breath class is a better start.

What to expect
Arrival and a short orientation: what kundalini activation is, what is normal, and how to opt out of anything
Progressive breath and movement rounds that build energy and heat
A peak where the practice is most active: emotion, shaking, heat, tingling, sound can all come up, all normal
A long, quiet integration: stillness, slow breath, nothing to do
A few minutes to land and share if you want to, before you leave
Benefits
A felt sense of energy moving where it had been stuck
Emotional release without needing a story for it
A reset for a system that has been running flat or wired-and-tired
A clearer, more spacious baseline for a day or two afterward

(No health claims. This is a practice, not a treatment.)

Pre-class prep
Skip heavy food and alcohol in the hours before.
Eat something light beforehand, not a full meal.
Come a few minutes early to settle
If you are pregnant, have a heart or blood-pressure condition, epilepsy, glaucoma, recent surgery, or are in acute mental-health crisis, message Lynn before booking so she can advise or adapt
Wear layers you can move in and get warm in.

Kundalini pranayama and breath of fire are intense. Please do not book, or check with Lynn first, if any of these apply: pregnancy, cardiovascular disease or uncontrolled high blood pressure, epilepsy or seizure history, glaucoma or detached retina, recent abdominal or chest surgery, acute psychosis or an unstable mental-health condition. Somatic breathwork to regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline in the body
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, deep rest, and integration, in a gentle, consent-based way
Life coaching to translate what opens in a session into grounded change in relationships, work, boundaries, and daily life

“A crisis is a terrible thing to waste” said famously by economist Paul Romer

Anxiety gets a bad reputation, but it's not actually the enemy. Anxiety is an internal alarm system, letting us know something in our life needs attention. We tend to respond by chasing the next fix that will soothe uncomfortable emotions, hoping the feeling will just go away. But if the underlying thing never gets addressed, the anxiety doesn't either. It just bubbles up in different ways and different situations.

This workshop isn't about adding another technique to your list. Instead, we'll look at how yoga lifestyle and yoga psychology approached this exact feeling long before self-care was a trend, and why that ancient framework still holds up today. Sometimes the answer isn't something new, it's remembering what already worked before and was simply overlooked.

A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, deep connection and brotherhood in a space of trust, presence and belonging.

Men’s Circle: Rooted in Connection




Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




The evening offers a supportive space for men to come together, connect, and speak openly about life. Whether you’re moving through a period of change, looking for deeper connection, or simply wanting a space where you can show up as you are, you’re welcome here.

The conversations are honest, open, and grounded in mutual respect. There’s no pressure to speak, share, or have everything figured out. You’re just as welcome to listen and be present. Together, we create a space rooted in confidentiality and non-judgement, where everyone can feel safe, heard, and free to be themselves.

Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.




After the circle, stay for a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert ($20 or $10 for students). Sharing a meal is a simple way to extend the sense of community and connection. This gathering is offered on a non-profit basis.
Meet Your Host: Sri Jiva

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

Cut through modern noise with Sivananda. Explore practical philosophy to tame distractions, strengthen focus, and find inner stability.

Inspire Me!
Master Your Attention: Practical philosophy to cut through modern noise

​Constant notifications, overthinking, and endless inputs make staying focused feel like a daily battle. In this workshop, we’ll dive into practical strategies alongside ancient psychological insights to help you tame distraction and find inner stability. Expect an open, conversation-driven space with Sivananda where you can ask questions and explore philosophy and real-world tools.




End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.




Meet your host Sivananda:

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

long_description:
Overview

Your mind is powerful but is it working for you? Join us for five practical tools that change how you think, feel and live every day.

Think Better, Live Better

A two-hour workshop that changes how you think

Most of us have never been taught how to think. We've learned what to think - at school, at work, through experience. But the actual process running in the background? The stories we tell ourselves, the patterns we fall into, the way we focus our attention, nobody really teaches that.

This workshop does.

Think Better, Live Better is a practical, engaging two-hour session grounded in real psychology and delivered in plain English. No jargon, no theory for theory's sake, and no forced positivity. Just five powerful tools you can start using the same day.

What you'll learn

Tool 1 — Change the story: Your brain defaults to the worst interpretation of any situation. Learn to catch that automatic story, question it, and replace it with a more accurate and useful one. This single shift reduces anxiety and improves decisions you make under pressure.

Tool 2 — Watch your own mind: Most of us are so inside our thoughts we never stop to look at them. This tool teaches you to step back and notice your own thinking patterns - the loops, the traps, the habits, without being swept along by them. Once you can name a pattern, you're no longer ruled by it.

Tool 3 — Get curious about what goes wrong: We've been taught to treat failure as evidence that something is wrong with us. This tool flips that. Learn to approach setbacks with curiosity rather than self-judgement, seeing the lesson, adjusting the approach, and moving forward with more confidence.

Tool 4 — Choose where your mind goes: Your brain is wired to scan for what's wrong three times more than it notices what's right. That's not a character flaw, it's biology. This tool teaches you to train your attention deliberately, so you're not at the mercy of stress, habit, and fear.

Tool 5 — Stop wrestling with your thoughts: Some thoughts don't need to be believed or fought, they just need to be noticed and let go. This tool gives you a simple, usable technique to unhook from the thoughts that hold you back, without trying to think them away.

What to expect

This is an interactive, conversational workshop, not a lecture. Expect real examples, honest discussion, a bit of laughter, and moments of reflection. Every participant receives a personal workbook to use during the session and take home, so you leave with something practical in your hands, not just in your head.

You'll finish the two hours with a complete inner toolkit and one clear commitment to yourself about how you'll use it.

This workshop is for you if:

you find yourself stuck in worry, self-doubt, or overthinking
you want to respond to pressure and setbacks more confidently
you're ready to have more control over how you think and feel
you're curious about how your mind works and ways to optimise it.

Workshop details

Duration: Two hours Includes: Personal workbook Group size: Intimate - maximum 12 participants Location: Wellington CBD

Come ready to be honest, curious, and a little bit surprised by what's possible.
